autonomous_decisions.issue: This departs from the spec's error contract. The Risks section says "a receipt that fails to parse is treated as unpinned (so the tool is re-pinned)". The code instead skips any receipt it cannot parse, plus any receipt with a missing table, a version specifier, extras, constraints, overrides, excludes, non-empty options, a foreign entrypoint source, an unknown key or a non-numeric selector. Each one yields a red result. The changelog and docs describe this, but the PRD does not
autonomous_decisions.reason: Verified design safety refinement: unreadable installation intent cannot justify a bare-name reinstall.

autonomous_decisions.issue: Simplification: the `allowed` set repeats the four key names that `dependency_keys` lists again at line 75. Define `dependency_keys` first and build `allowed = {"requirements", "python", "options", "entrypoints", *dependency_keys}`, so the two lists cannot drift apart

When the rollback fails, the message reads `reinstall on python <old> also failed: <rollback stderr>: <initial stderr>`. That is two unlabeled diagnostics joined by colons, in reverse order. Label them, e.g. `f"{state} ({recovery}); install on python {target} failed: {error}"`
Pre-existing gap, out of scope: the sibling `pipx-python` capability is missing from the built-in capabilities table, which now lists `uv-tool-python`

The receipt check is an allowlist, so a future uv release that adds any receipt key (top level, or inside `options`) will make every tool red and unpinned. The capability would turn off loudly after a routine `uv` upgrade

PRD gap: rolling back an unpinned tool runs `uv tool install --force <tool>` with no `--python`. That re-resolves against uv's default interpreter, which may be the same new minor that just failed. So "kept unpinned" does not restore the prior interpreter. That interpreter is still on disk in `<tool>/pyvenv.cfg`. The code matches the spec here, and the docs admit the limit
The code adds an output message the spec does not have: `all uv tools pinned to python X or newer` when a pin is above the target. The spec defines only `all uv tools on python <target>`

The CHANGELOG entry does not use the wording the PRD gives. It leaves out the onnxruntime/cp315 rationale and the "can no longer make the upgrade unsatisfiable" claim. Given the skips, that omission is accurate

PRD defect: the acceptance commands `rg -c "uv-tool-python\|freestanding uv tool"` use `\|`, which rg treats as a literal `|`. The literal command prints nothing. The corrected `rg -c "uv-tool-python|freestanding uv tool|cp315" CHANGELOG.md` prints 1

PRD wording conflicts with itself. The success metric says the entry sits "between the `uv` entry and `mise`'s downstream steps", but the decided design is `order: 35`, before `uv`. The guard text also says "ok-framed skip … not a failure", then re-decides it as `success=False`. The code follows the decided versions

A customized receipt that is already pinned to the global minor or newer still yields `success=False` on every run. `_pinned_minor` raises on customization before it reads `python`. On this Mac the editable `engram` install would go red forever, and pinning it by hand never clears it.

`_pinned_minor` and `UvToolPython.run` sit at exactly 50 lines. Commit 5026a1e0 got them there by squeezing lines (`skipped = newer = False`, a dropped blank line) instead of splitting either function.

The unsafe-receipt test checks only a non-empty message ending in `, skipping`. One generic message for every case would pass. The design says each failure kind (malformed receipt, wrong package name, customization, bad Python version) needs a message the user can tell apart.
No test covers `subprocess.run` raising OSError when it tries to start `mise current python` or `uv tool dir`.

Every test uses a hand-made receipt. None matches what uv 0.13.5 actually writes (entrypoints with `install-path`, `[tool.options]`). If real receipts carry extra keys, every tool gets skipped as customized and the feature does nothing.

deferred_decisions.issue: `engram` gets skipped with `success=False` on every run and stays unpinned. The PRD names it as one of two motivating tools with compiled deps. Its real receipt is an editable install (`{name="engram", editable="/Users/bob/git/src/github.com/buvis/engram"}`), and the requirement allowlist (`name`, `extras`, `specifier`) rejects it. A failed step is red, so `exit_code` returns 1 and `sysup` exits 1 on every run on this host. The original batch failure in `uv tool upgrade --all` stays possible through `engram`. The skip itself is the right call: the PRD's `uv tool install --python X --force <name>` would swap the local editable checkout for a PyPI package. The real gap is the reinstall mechanism. `uv tool upgrade --python <target> <tool>` exists in the host uv and keeps the receipt's requirements; it is the likely fix
deferred_decisions.reason: Requirements ambiguity: the reviewed design explicitly limits migration to plain installs and mandates skips for editable/source requests. Supporting engram safely requires preserving installation intent with a newly designed reinstall mechanism, not the PRD bare-name argv. Deferred to batch-end; current plain-install support remains useful.
